tagline.value: A group trip planner for any trip and any group. Invite-only, phone-first, and built so a different trip, group size or budget does not turn into clutter. A Japan trip was the first real use.

cover.request: A screenshot of the sign-in screen, or sanitised app screens with no trip data, names or invite codes.

genre.value: Group trip planner (not a game) — multipurpose product and UX case study

value: Designed and built Tabi: more than one trip on an account, each with its own invite-only group (viewer and editor roles); a day-by-day itinerary with map pins; a budget with a whole-group / per-person toggle and a budget-ceiling warning; live currency conversion; weather; a home screen that shows Today's plan during a trip and a countdown before it; Google sign-in.
Designed and built the earlier screens too: sign-in gate, trip overview, budget, plan, stays, flights, food, trains and people.
Reworked most of the code and the visual design to get a mobile-first, phone-app feel.
Iterated in small pull requests: 60 over eight days, 57 merged.
contributions.source: Owner, 29 Sep 2026, 00:36 AEST, from the build history. Designer and developer, solo.

problem.value: One app has to serve any trip and any group. The plan and the money need to live together, and the app has to stay clear when the trip, the group size and the budget all change. A Japan trip was the first real use, often checked on a phone.
problem.source: Owner, 29 Sep 2026, 00:36 AEST. The first-use setting is from the earlier build history.

designGoal.value: Make one planner flexible across different trips, group sizes and budgets without clutter, and never blur money that is certain with money that is a guess.
designGoal.source: Owner, 29 Sep 2026, 00:36 AEST, plus the earlier money-state goal from the build history.

intended.value: Before a trip, the home screen is a countdown. During a trip, it is Today's plan. A Japan trip was the first real use of that.

value: Mobile-first layout with a bottom bar per section and a single + that adds anything from anywhere.
Three money states on every cost — paid, committed, estimated — that always add up to the projected total.
'Still to sort' health check listing only what needs a look (nights with nowhere to stay, payments due, missing prices).
'What changed?' line after an edit, e.g. projected cost before → after.

evidence.request: How the group actually used it: what they checked most, what confused them, what you changed (no personal data).

decisions.decision: Never show a guess as if it were certain
decisions.detail: Every cost is marked paid, committed (booked, not fully paid) or estimated, and the three always add up to the projected cost. With no budget set, the app says 'No budget set' rather than inventing a figure.

why.value: Money a group has actually spent and money it might spend lead to different decisions; mixing them hides risk.
why.source: Build history, read-only ('never blurs money that is certain with money that is a guess')

evidence.request: What prompted this (e.g. a confusing total).

result.value: Added in the 'precise money states' iteration (PR #56) and carried onto the plan (PR #59).

decisions.detail: A gate is a field filled in on the day through a deliberately small form, and the app records when it was set. A live-status link sits beside it; flights without a number say so instead of showing a dead button.

why.value: Airports assign gates a few hours before departure, so the app doesn't pretend to know — and a gate from yesterday is worse than no gate at all.

decisions.detail: Accounts are created only from an invite that a trip owner issues; sign-in is through Google.

why.value: The app holds a private group's plans and payments; nobody should be able to wander in.
why.source: Tyler (owner confirmation, 28 Sep 2026) + Build history, read-only

options.value: Password sign-in and Apple Sign In were tried; Apple was removed (PR #21), then sign-in was made Google-only (PR #24).

tradeoff.request: What it costs a traveller without a Google account.

decisions.detail: Guests see a flight's route, times, terminal and gate, but never the fare, seat or booking reference.

why.value: A booking reference plus a surname is often enough to change or cancel a booking.

decisions.detail: Off by default, with a timer and a blur setting, and only visible to people on the same trip.

why.request: Why you designed it this way (in your words).

image.request: Screenshot of an early build (no trip data)

what.value: Feature build-out: a budget against a group target, live currency conversion (the first trip, a Japan trip, used AUD and JPY), a Today view, and maps (PRs #1–26).

why.request: What you learned from the first version

what.value: 'Budget-first, mobile-first redesign' (PR #27), then 'a full visual redesign' (PR #28).
Design pass: trip pass, departure board, route strip, payments to approve (PR #54).
Precise money states, honest empty states, trips on their own clock, daily backups (PRs #55–60).

item.request: Who used or tested it (e.g. the travel group), no names needed

results.request: How it's being used (only real, non-personal facts).

reflection.value: The design challenge is one app that stays flexible across different trips, group sizes and budgets without clutter. Tabi keeps each trip in its own invite-only group, breaks the plan into days with map pins, and lets the same budget be read for the whole group or per person, with a warning at the ceiling. The home screen changes job: a countdown before the trip, Today's plan during it. A Japan trip was the first real use. It was the test case, not a limit on who the app is for.
